title.en: Volume 449 Biographies 236: Xi Liang, Zhou Fu, Lu Yuanding, Zhang Cengyang, Yang Shixiang, Feng Xu
title.raw: 卷449 列傳二百三十六 锡良 周馥 陆元鼎 张曾敭 杨士骧 冯煦

sentences.zh: 列傳二百三十六

translations.literal: Biographies 236
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 236

sentences.zh: 錫良周馥陸元鼎張曾敭楊士驤馮煦

translations.literal: Xi Liang, Zhou Fu, Lu Yuanding, Zhang Cengyang, Yang Shixiang, and Feng Xu
translations.idiomatic: [Biographies of] Xi Liang, Zhou Fu, Lu Yuanding, Zhang Cengyang, Yang Shixiang, and Feng Xu

sentences.zh: 錫良，字清弼，巴岳特氏，蒙古鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Xi Liang, courtesy name Qingbi, of the Bayuete clan, was a Mongol of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang, whose courtesy name was Qingbi, belonged to the Bayuete clan and was a Mongol bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，用山西知縣，歷任州縣有惠政。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a Shanxi county magistrate; in successive prefectural and county posts he carried out benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in 1874 and was assigned as a county magistrate in Shanxi, where his successive posts at the prefectural and county level were marked by policies that benefited the people.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，晉大旱，錫良歷辦賑務，戶必清查，款必實放，民皆德之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign Shanxi suffered a great drought; Xi Liang repeatedly handled relief work, every household was surely investigated, funds were surely actually disbursed, and the people all regarded him with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign, when Shanxi was stricken by severe drought, Xi Liang oversaw relief again and again: every household was checked, every disbursement was paid out in full, and the people came to esteem him for it.

sentences.zh: 二十年，山東巡撫李秉衡奏調補沂州知府，擢兗沂曹濟道。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year [of Guangxu], Shandong governor Li Bingheng memorialized to transfer him to fill the post of Yizhou prefect, and he was promoted to the Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, Shandong Governor Li Bingheng had him transferred to serve as prefect of Yizhou, after which he was promoted intendant of the Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji Circuit.

sentences.zh: 抵任，值單縣大刀會滋事，亟率隊往，張示諭眾，祗擒首要，搜獲盟單，當眾焚之，匪黨感畏，皆散。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post, it happened that the Dadaohui in Shan County stirred up trouble; he urgently led troops there, posted proclamations to instruct the crowd, arrested only the ringleaders, searched out and seized alliance registers, burned them before the assembly, and the bandit party, moved to fear, all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took office, the Big Sword Society in Shan County rose in disturbance. He hurried there at the head of a detachment, posted notices to the crowd, seized only the ringleaders, recovered the society's membership rolls, and burned them in public; awed by this, the rebels all melted away.

sentences.zh: 調山西冀寧道，晉按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Shanxi Jining Circuit, then promoted provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Jining Circuit in Shanxi and then promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 調湖南，擢布政使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hunan, he was promoted provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: After a transfer to Hunan, he was elevated to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳亂召禍，京師危急。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer turmoil summoned disaster and the capital was critically imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the Boxer uprising brought catastrophe, and the capital stood in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 錫良以湖廣總督、湖北湖南巡撫會委，統率鄂、湘軍隊入衛，迎駕山西，立授巡撫。

translations.literal: Xi Liang, as concurrently governor-general of Huguang and jointly commissioned governor of Hubei and Hunan, commanded Hubei and Hunan troops to enter for defense, received the imperial progress in Shanxi, and was immediately appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: As governor-general of Huguang and concurrently commissioned to govern Hubei and Hunan, Xi Liang led troops from those provinces to escort the court into Shanxi and was at once appointed governor of the province.

sentences.zh: 時和議未定，洋兵闌入晉邊。

translations.literal: At the time peace negotiations were not yet settled, and foreign troops intruded into the Shanxi border.
translations.idiomatic: Peace talks were still unsettled when foreign forces crossed into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 錫良念兩宮幸陝，和局固應兼顧，而保晉衛秦，亦不容忽。

translations.literal: Xi Liang reflected that the two palaces had gone in fortune to Shaanxi: the peace settlement certainly had to be kept in view, yet defending Shanxi and guarding Shaanxi could not be neglected either.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang reasoned that with the empress dowager and emperor sheltered in Shaanxi, the peace negotiations had to be watched—but securing Shanxi and shielding the road to Shaanxi could not be slighted either.

sentences.zh: 乃通令各軍嚴行防守，別遣委員出境犒師，相機因應，幸保無事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued a general order to all armies to enforce defense strictly, separately dispatched commissioners beyond the border to present gifts to the troops, and adapted measures as circumstances allowed; by good fortune peace was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all units to hold their defenses firmly, sent commissioners across the border to offer gifts to the foreign armies, and adjusted his response as events unfolded—so that, fortunately, the province escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 和約定，晉始弛防。

translations.literal: When the treaty was fixed, Shanxi only then relaxed its defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the treaty was signed did Shanxi stand down from full alert.

sentences.zh: 調湖北巡撫，復開缺。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hubei as governor, he again had his post declared vacant [for reassignment].
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as governor of Hubei, then left the post open again when moved elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 旋授河南河道總督。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed director-general of the Henan waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed director-general of Henan river conservancy.

sentences.zh: 以事簡，奏請裁歸巡撫兼理，詔允行。

translations.literal: Because the duties were simple, he memorialized to abolish the office and return its affairs to the governor for concurrent management; an edict approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the post's duties light, he memorialized to abolish it and fold river work into the governor's portfolio; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 調補河南巡撫，兼管河工。

translations.literal: Transferred to fill the Henan governorship, he concurrently supervised river works.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as governor of Henan and also took charge of river conservancy.

sentences.zh: 豫省吏治久隳，劾去道府以次數十人，政紀肅然。

translations.literal: Henan provincial administration had long been ruined; he impeached and removed several tens of persons from circuit intendant and prefect downward, and governmental discipline became austere.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's officialdom had long been corrupt; he impeached and dismissed dozens of officials from circuit intendant down through the prefectural ranks, and administrative discipline was sharply restored.

sentences.zh: 泌陽教案事起，立派兵馳捕首犯，被擾難民，無分民教，一律撫卹。

translations.literal: When the Biyang missionary-case incident arose, he immediately dispatched troops to hurry and seize the chief culprits; refugees who had suffered disturbance, without distinction of layman or convert, were all alike comforted and compensated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Biyang missionary-case affair broke out, he at once sent troops to hunt down the ringleaders and compensated every refugee who had suffered—Christian or not—without distinction.

sentences.zh: 調熱河都統。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Rehe governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Rehe governor-general.

sentences.zh: 熱河本就蒙地設治，向沿舊習，不講吏事，尤患多盜。

translations.literal: Rehe had originally been administered as territory set up on Mongol lands; it had always followed old customs, did not attend to civil administration, and above all suffered from many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Rehe had been governed as administration on Mongol territory, where old customs prevailed, civil routine was neglected, and banditry was especially rife.

sentences.zh: 錫良首請改制，設立求治局，綜理吏治財政；

translations.literal: Xi Liang was the first to request institutional reform, establishing a Bureau for Seeking Good Government to oversee civil administration and finance;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang was the first to press for institutional reform, establishing a Bureau for Seeking Good Government to coordinate civil administration and revenue;

sentences.zh: 開辦圍場荒地，以興墾務；

translations.literal: opened waste land in the imperial hunting enclosures to promote reclamation;
translations.idiomatic: opened waste land in the imperial hunting grounds to promote reclamation;

sentences.zh: 整飭巡防，專意緝捕，匪風始戢。

translations.literal: rectified patrol defense, devoted his mind solely to pursuit and arrest, and the bandit wind only then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: reorganized patrol forces and focused on arrests until banditry finally abated.

sentences.zh: 又以熱境地廣官少，奏請升朝陽縣為府，並增設阜新、建平、隆化三縣，熱河自此始有吏治。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Rehe's territory was broad and officials few, he memorialized to raise Chaoyang County to a prefecture and additionally establish the three counties of Fuxin, Jianping, and Longhua; from this Rehe first had civil administration.
translations.idiomatic: Because Rehe was vast yet thinly staffed, he memorialized to elevate Chaoyang County to a prefecture and to add the counties of Fuxin, Jianping, and Longhua—marking the point at which Rehe finally acquired a real civil administration.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，擢閩浙總督，調署四川。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang and transferred to act as governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1903 he was promoted governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang and transferred to serve as acting governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時方議借外款修川路，錫良力主自辦，集紳會議，奏設專局，招商股，籌公股，复就通省田租歲抽百分之三，名為租股，數年積至千萬以上，股款之多，為中國自辦鐵路最。

translations.literal: At the time they were just discussing borrowing foreign funds to build the Sichuan railway; Xi Liang strongly advocated self-management, gathered the gentry for conference, memorialized to establish a special bureau, solicited merchant shares and planned public shares, and further from the province-wide land tax annually drew three percent, called rent shares; within several years accumulation reached more than ten million, the share funds being the greatest among China's self-managed railways.
translations.idiomatic: While officials debated borrowing foreign capital for the Sichuan railway, Xi Liang insisted on a Chinese-run project: he convened the local gentry, memorialized for a dedicated bureau, raised merchant and public subscriptions, and levied an annual three-percent surcharge on provincial land tax called "rent shares." Within a few years subscriptions passed ten million taels—the largest fund ever raised for a domestically financed railway in China.

sentences.zh: 三十年，廷議整飭藏事，藏人疑懼，駐藏幫辦鳳全被戕。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the court discussed rectifying Tibetan affairs; Tibetans were suspicious and fearful, and Feng Quan, assistant commissioner in Tibet, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1904 the court debated tightening control over Tibet; Tibetans grew fearful, and Feng Quan, the assistant commissioner in Lhasa, was murdered.

sentences.zh: 錫良飛檄提督馬維騏督兵進剿，並令建昌道趙爾豐率師繼進，遂克巴塘，仍飭爾豐進討里塘。

translations.literal: Xi Liang sent flying dispatches ordering Provincial Commander Ma Weiqi to supervise troops in advance suppression, and also ordered Jianchang Circuit Intendant Zhao Erfeng to lead the army in continued advance; they thereupon captured Batang and he still ordered Erfeng to advance and attack Litang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang urgently ordered Provincial Commander Ma Weiqi to lead a punitive campaign and directed Jianchang Intendant Zhao Erfeng to follow with reinforcements. Batang was taken, and Xi Liang then ordered Zhao to press on against Litang.

sentences.zh: 裡屬桑披寺築碉謀抗拒，爾豐以長圍困守六閱月，斷其汲道，始克攻破。

translations.literal: In Litang territory Sangpi Monastery built blockhouses plotting resistance; Erfeng with a long siege penned them for six months, cut off their water route, and only then succeeded in storming and breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: Near Litang, Sangpi Monastery built fortifications to resist; Zhao Erfeng invested it for six months, cut off its water supply, and finally stormed it successfully.

sentences.zh: 桑寺既平，諸番忄習服。

translations.literal: Once Sang Monastery was pacified, the various tribes all submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: With Sangpi Monastery subdued, the Tibetan tribes submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 於是自打箭爐以外，直至察木多、巴里、鄉​​城、德格等處，均改縣治，擴地至數千馀裡；

translations.literal: Thereupon from beyond Dartsedo as far as Chamdo, Pari, Xiangcheng, Dêgê, and other places, all were changed to county administration, expanding territory to several thousand-odd li;
translations.idiomatic: From Dartsedo westward through Chamdo, Pari, Xiangcheng, Dêgê, and beyond, county administration was extended over several thousand li of newly organized territory;

sentences.zh: 且興墾、開礦，設學廣教，番人漸知向化矣。

translations.literal: moreover reclamation was promoted, mines opened, schools established and instruction spread abroad, and the tribesmen gradually came to know orientation toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: reclamation, mining, schools, and wider instruction followed, and the frontier peoples gradually turned toward civilization.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，調雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1907 he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 滇省軍政久廢，器械尤缺，乃創練陸軍，設講武堂，添購槍砲，舊有防營一律改編，自是滇省始有新軍。

translations.literal: Yunnan's military administration had long been abandoned and weapons especially lacking; he thereupon created training of the army, established a military academy, added purchases of guns and cannon, and uniformly reorganized the old defense battalions—from this Yunnan first had a new army.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's military establishment had long decayed and arms were especially scarce. He raised a modern army, founded a military academy, purchased rifles and artillery, and reorganized the old defense battalions—giving Yunnan its first new-style force.

sentences.zh: 滇多煙產，土稅為收入大宗，錫良毅然奏請禁種，各省煙禁之嚴，唯滇為最。

translations.literal: Yunnan had much opium production and the native tax was a major portion of revenue; Xi Liang resolutely memorialized to forbid cultivation; among the provinces' opium prohibitions, only Yunnan's was strictest.
translations.idiomatic: Opium was a major Yunnan crop and its land tax a main revenue source, yet Xi Liang boldly memorialized to ban cultivation outright. Of all provincial anti-opium measures, Yunnan's was the strictest.

sentences.zh: 滇南連越，越匪竄入河口，戕官擾境，立飭出隊分路截剿，數日而定。

translations.literal: Yunnan's south adjoined Annam; Annamese bandits slipped into Hekou, killed officials and disturbed the border; he immediately ordered troops out on separate routes to intercept and suppress, and within several days it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Along Yunnan's southern border with Vietnam, bandits crossed at Hekou, killed officials, and raided the frontier. He immediately sent columns by separate routes to cut them off; within days the disturbance was ended.

sentences.zh: 滇西土司以數十計，​​日漸恣橫。

translations.literal: Western Yunnan's native chieftains numbered in the several tens and daily grew more willful and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yunnan had dozens of native chieftains who grew more arrogant by the day.

sentences.zh: 宣慰使刁安仁曾遊東洋，外人稱以王爵，尤驕妄。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Diao Anren had once traveled to Japan; foreigners addressed him with princely title, and he was especially proud and reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Diao Anren had visited Japan, where foreigners addressed him as royalty; he was especially haughty and reckless.

sentences.zh: 聞有改土歸流之議，輒思蠢動。

translations.literal: Hearing talk of replacing native rule with regular administration, he would at once think to stir up trouble foolishly.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard proposals to replace native chieftain rule with direct administration, he was ready to stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 錫良先派員詢察，曉以利害，並令應襲各土司迅辦承襲，以安其心。

translations.literal: Xi Liang first dispatched officers to inquire and investigate, explained advantage and harm, and also ordered each chieftain due to succeed to hurry and complete succession installation, to settle their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang first sent investigators to explain the stakes, and ordered every eligible chieftain to complete succession promptly so as to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 刁安仁聞而畏感，遣其弟至，痛哭自陳改悔，邊境得以無事。

translations.literal: Diao Anren, on hearing, was moved to fear and gratitude, sent his younger brother to come, wept bitterly and himself stated repentance; the borderland was thereby able to be without incident.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Anren, awed and moved, sent his brother to prostrate himself in tears and pledge repentance, and the frontier remained quiet.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，授欽差大臣，調東三省總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was appointed imperial commissioner and transferred to governor-general of the Three Eastern Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909 he was appointed imperial commissioner and transferred to governor-general of the Three Eastern Provinces (Manchuria).

sentences.zh: 東省自日俄戰罷，俄佔北邊，日踞南境，局勢日危。

translations.literal: Since the Russo-Japanese War ended in the Eastern Provinces, Russia occupied the northern border and Japan held the southern marches; the situation daily grew perilous.
translations.idiomatic: After the Russo-Japanese War, Russia held the north of Manchuria and Japan the south, and the region grew more precarious by the day.

sentences.zh: 錫良蒞任，即疏陳：「東三省逼邇京畿，關係大局。

translations.literal: When Xi Liang arrived to take office, he immediately memorialized: 'The Three Eastern Provinces press close upon the capital region and concern the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Xi Liang at once memorialized: "The Three Eastern Provinces lie hard against the capital and bear on the fate of the empire.

sentences.zh: 遼東租借之約，十三年即滿期，請朝廷主持，上下一心，以天下全力赴之，以贖回遼東半島為歸，否則枝枝節節為之，恐其不能及也。

translations.literal: The Liaodong lease treaty in thirteen years will reach its term; I beg the court to take charge, above and below of one mind, with the whole empire's full strength applied to it, taking recovery of the Liaodong peninsula as the return—otherwise, doing it branch by branch and joint by joint, I fear it cannot be reached in time.'
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong lease expires in thirteen years. I beg the throne to take the lead, unite court and country, and commit the empire's full strength to recovering the Liaodong peninsula. Otherwise, if we tackle it piecemeal, I fear we shall not finish in time."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，不省。

translations.literal: ' The memorial entered and was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went in and received no response.

sentences.zh: 錫良又以東三省兩鄰分據，非脩大支干路，不足以貫串脈絡，因擬修錦州至璦琿鐵路。

translations.literal: Xi Liang also, because the Two Eastern Provinces' neighbors divided occupation, [said that] without building a great trunk line one could not thread the veins and arteries; he therefore planned to build the railway from Jinzhou to Aihui.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang argued that with Russia and Japan dividing the region, only a major trunk line could tie Manchuria together, and proposed a railway from Jinzhou to Aihui.

sentences.zh: 顧須橫貫南滿、東清，必非日、俄所原，尤非密借強國外款，不能取均勢而策進行。

translations.literal: But it had to cross southern Manchuria and the Chinese Eastern Railway—surely not what Japan and Russia desired; especially without secretly borrowing foreign funds from a strong power, one could not take balanced advantage and plan advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the line would cross southern Manchuria and the Chinese Eastern Railway—something neither Japan nor Russia would welcome—and could advance only by secretly borrowing from a great power to balance their interests.

sentences.zh: 適美國財團代表遊歷來奉，遂與密訂借款包修草約。

translations.literal: It happened that an American financial-group representative was touring and came to Fengtian; he thereupon secretly concluded a draft agreement for a loan and contracted construction.
translations.idiomatic: An American syndicate representative happened to be touring Manchuria, and Xi Liang secretly drew up a draft loan-and-construction agreement with him.

sentences.zh: 三日議定，電奏請旨速正式簽定，即日、俄再爭，已落後著。

translations.literal: In three days it was settled; he telegraphed a memorial requesting imperial approval to speed formal signing—even if Japan and Russia disputed again, one would already be a move behind.
translations.idiomatic: Terms were settled in three days; he telegraphed Beijing to authorize formal signing at once—otherwise, even if Japan and Russia fought over the line again, China would already be one move behind.

sentences.zh: 乃部議梗緩，復機事不密，事竟報罷。

translations.literal: But the ministry's deliberations were obstructive and slow, and again the affair was not kept secret; the matter in the end was reported abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial deliberations dragged, the plan leaked, and the project was finally abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及日俄協約，東事益急。

translations.literal: When the Japan-Russia agreement came, Eastern affairs grew still more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Russo-Japanese agreement, the eastern crisis grew still more acute.

sentences.zh: 錫良以救亡興政，均非款莫辦，再請商借二千萬兩，以千萬設銀行；

translations.literal: Xi Liang, holding that saving the nation and promoting government both could not be done without funds, again requested to negotiate borrowing twenty million taels, using ten million to establish a bank;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang held that national salvation and reform alike required capital, and again proposed borrowing twenty million taels—ten million for a bank;

sentences.zh: 其馀，半以移民興墾，半以開礦築路。

translations.literal: the remainder, half for immigration and promoting reclamation, half for opening mines and building railways.
translations.idiomatic: the rest to be split between colonization and reclamation on one hand and mining and railways on the other.

sentences.zh: 仍不省。

translations.literal: Still it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Again the court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 錫良慮東省危急情形，朝廷尚未深悉，乃請入覲面陳。

translations.literal: Xi Liang feared the Eastern Provinces' critical perilous situation was not yet deeply understood at court; he thereupon requested audience to state it in person.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the court did not fully grasp Manchuria's peril, Xi Liang asked leave to present the case in person at audience.

sentences.zh: 時醇親王監國攝攻，籌備立憲，廷議方注重集權。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Chun supervised the state as regent, preparing constitutional government; court discussion was just then emphasizing centralization of power.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chun was regent, constitutional government was being prepared, and court debate favored centralization.

sentences.zh: 錫良先疏請實行憲法，歷陳：「立憲精神，在貴賤上下胥受治於法律，先革其自私自利之心。

translations.literal: Xi Liang first memorialized requesting implementation of the constitution, setting forth in detail: 'The spirit of constitutional government lies in noble and base, above and below, all alike receiving governance under law—first reform the heart of selfish profit-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang first memorialized for a real constitution, arguing: "Constitutional government means that high and low alike live under law—we must first uproot selfishness.

sentences.zh: 若敷衍掊克，似是而非，財力凋敝，人心渙漓，九年立憲，終恐為波斯之續。

translations.literal: If one is perfunctory and extorts, seeming so yet not so, financial strength withers, popular hearts scatter and dissolve—in nine years' constitutionalism one ultimately fears becoming Persia's sequel.'
translations.idiomatic: If we offer a sham constitution while squeezing the people, wealth will fail and loyalty dissolve—and the nine-year timetable may end like Persia's constitutional experiment."

sentences.zh: 」又以近年重臣親貴出洋考察，徒飾觀聽，見輕外人，疏請停派，並慎選親貴實行留學。

translations.literal: ' He also, because in recent years great ministers and imperial kinsmen went abroad on inspection tours merely to ornament appearances and were looked down on by foreigners, memorialized to stop dispatching them, and carefully select imperial kinsmen to carry out study abroad in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged an end to sending grandees abroad on ceremonial inspection tours that foreigners mocked, and instead to choose princes for serious study overseas.

sentences.zh: 再疏諫中央集權，以為：「朝廷分寄事權於督撫，猶督撫分寄事權於州縣，無州縣即督撫不能治一省。

translations.literal: Again he memorialized remonstrating against central concentration of power, holding: 'The court delegates administrative authority to governors-general and governors just as governors-general and governors delegate authority to prefectures and counties—without prefectures and counties, governors cannot govern a province.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again against centralization: "The court delegates power to governors just as governors delegate to prefects and magistrates—without the latter, no governor can run a province.

sentences.zh: 如必欲以數部臣之心思才力，統治二十二行省，則疆吏咸為贅旒，風氣所趨，軍民解體。

translations.literal: If one must use the minds and talents of a few ministry ministers to govern twenty-two provinces, then frontier officials all become superfluous appendages; where the wind of custom trends, army and people disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: If a handful of ministry officials must govern all twenty-two provinces, frontier governors become ornaments, morale collapses, and army and people fall apart.

sentences.zh: 設有緩急，中央既耳目不及，外省則呼應不靈，為患實大。

translations.literal: Suppose there is urgency: the center already cannot reach with eyes and ears, the outer provinces then cannot respond nimbly—the harm is truly great.'
translations.idiomatic: In an emergency the center cannot see or hear, and the provinces cannot act—the harm would be grave."

sentences.zh: 」均不報。

translations.literal: ' None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: " None of these memorials was answered.

sentences.zh: 至是，入都面陳監國，語尤切直，不省如故。

translations.literal: At this point, entering the capital he stated face to face to the regent; his words were especially cutting and direct—still not heeded as before.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital and spoke to the regent in person, his words were especially blunt—and still went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 告罷，又不允。

translations.literal: He asked to retire and was again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign and was again refused.

sentences.zh: 其時朝鮮為日並，錫良以事勢益迫，欲固民心，先厚民力，當以防匪為名，設立清鄉局，籌備預備巡警，部以兵法，實即民兵。

translations.literal: At that time Korea was annexed by Japan; Xi Liang, because the situation grew still more pressing, wished to solidify popular hearts and first enrich popular strength; under the name of guarding against bandits he established rural pacification bureaus, prepared reserve constabulary, organized them by military law—in reality they were militia.
translations.idiomatic: Korea had just been annexed by Japan. Seeing the crisis tighten, Xi Liang sought to strengthen popular loyalty by strengthening popular resources: under the pretext of bandit suppression he set up rural pacification bureaus and trained reserve constables by military drill—in effect a militia.

sentences.zh: 奉人慮患思痛，爭先應募，期年得數萬人，全省皆兵。

translations.literal: Fengtian people, anxious over disaster and mindful of pain, vied to enlist first; within a year he obtained several tens of thousands, and the whole province was soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by the danger, the people of Fengtian rushed to enlist; within a year he had tens of thousands, and the province was effectively armed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，防疫事起，疫起俄境，沿東清鐵路，逐處傳染，未浹旬，蔓延奉、吉、黑三省。

translations.literal: Before long epidemic prevention arose; the epidemic began on the Russian border, along the Chinese Eastern Railway spread infection place by place, and within less than ten days it spread through Fengtian, Jilin, and Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a plague broke out on the Russian border and spread along the Chinese Eastern Railway; in less than ten days it covered Fengtian, Jilin, and Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 俄、日群思干涉，錫良以防疫純屬內政，嚴起防治，三月而疫絕。

translations.literal: Russia and Japan all thought to interfere; Xi Liang held epidemic prevention was purely internal government, strictly launched prevention and treatment, and in three months the epidemic ended.
translations.idiomatic: Russia and Japan both sought to intervene, but Xi Liang insisted that epidemic control was purely a domestic matter, imposed strict measures, and extinguished the outbreak in three months.

sentences.zh: 十一國醫士來奉考察，開萬國鼠疫研究會於省署，錫良主議，咸起頌之。

translations.literal: Physicians from eleven countries came to Fengtian to investigate; an International Plague Research Congress was opened at the provincial yamen, Xi Liang presided over deliberations, and all rose to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians from eleven countries came to Fengtian to study the outbreak; Xi Liang chaired an international plague conference at the provincial government, winning widespread praise.

sentences.zh: 錫良督東，嚴吏治，肅軍制，清理財政，整頓鹽務，籌辦八旗生計，頗著成績。

translations.literal: Xi Liang governed the East, tightened civil administration, rectified military discipline, cleared finances, put salt administration in order, planned livelihood for the Eight Banners, and achieved considerable results.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of the East, Xi Liang tightened civil administration and military discipline, cleaned up finances, reformed the salt monopoly, and addressed Banner livelihood—with notable results.

sentences.zh: 唯目睹內憂外患日危一日，顧所以為東邊計者，既多未如志，而朝政日非，民心日去，又無以挽救，屢稱病乞罷。

translations.literal: Only he witnessed internal worry and external peril daily more perilous by a day; as for plans for the eastern border, many had already not matched his will, while court government daily worsened and popular hearts daily departed—again with no means to rescue; he repeatedly pleaded illness to beg dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he watched internal troubles and foreign threats worsen daily; most of his plans for the northeast had failed, court politics decayed, and popular loyalty ebbed with nothing he could do to stop it—so he repeatedly pleaded illness to resign.

sentences.zh: 三年，始允解任調理。

translations.literal: In the third year [of Xuantong] he was at last permitted to leave office for recuperation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911 he was finally allowed to leave office for medical leave.

sentences.zh: 武昌變作，召入覲，廷議本以錫良赴山、陝督師，並請獨領一軍衛京畿。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang uprising occurred, he was summoned to audience; court deliberation originally intended Xi Liang to go to Shanxi and Shaanxi to supervise the army, and also requested he alone lead an army to guard the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuchang revolt broke out he was summoned to court, which had planned to send him to command in Shanxi and Shaanxi and also to lead a separate force to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 顧有人惎之，乃改授熱河都統，力疾赴任。

translations.literal: But someone slandered him; he was then changed to appointment as Rehe governor-general and, forcing himself despite illness, went to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies slandered him, however, and he was reassigned instead as Rehe governor-general, which he took up despite grave illness.

sentences.zh: 遜位詔下，以病勢難支，乞罷，允之。

translations.literal: When the abdication edict was issued, because his illness was hard to sustain, he begged dismissal and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication edict he pleaded that his illness was beyond bearing and was permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 臥病六年，堅拒醫藥，卒，年六十有六，諡文誠。

translations.literal: He lay ill six years, firmly refused medicine, and died at age sixty-six; posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He remained bedridden for six years, refusing medicine to the end, and died at sixty-six; his posthumous title was Wencheng (Cultivated Sincerity).

sentences.zh: 錫良性清剛，自官牧令，即挺立無所倚。

translations.literal: Xi Liang's nature was pure and firm; from the time he served as prefectural and county magistrate he stood upright without relying on anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang was upright and unyielding; from his first magistracy he stood on his own without patrons.

sentences.zh: 嫉惡嚴，所蒞止，遇不職官吏，劾治不少卹；

translations.literal: His hatred of evil was severe; wherever he arrived and stopped, encountering unworthy officials he impeached and punished without sparing;
translations.idiomatic: He hated corruption fiercely; wherever he served he impeached incompetent officials without mercy;

sentences.zh: 非義之財，一介不取；

translations.literal: unrighteous wealth, not one cash would he take;
translations.idiomatic: he would not accept a single cash of ill-gotten money;

sentences.zh: 於權貴尤一無饋遺，故遇事動相牽制雲。

translations.literal: toward the powerful and noble especially he made not one gift; therefore when matters arose he was constantly mutually obstructed, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: and he never offered gifts to the powerful—so, it was said, they constantly obstructed him.

sentences.zh: 周馥，字玉山，安徽建德人。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu, courtesy name Yushan, was a native of Jiande, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, whose courtesy name was Yushan, came from Jiande in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初侍李鴻章司文牘，累保道員。

translations.literal: At first he attended Li Hongzhang managing documents, and through successive promotions reached circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a secretary to Li Hongzhang and rose by successive promotion to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，署永定河道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he acted as Yongding River director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877 he served as acting director of the Yongding River conservancy.

sentences.zh: 初，天津頻患水，馥迭治津沽入海金鐘河、北運筐港減河及通州潮白河，設文武汛官資防守。

translations.literal: At first Tianjin frequently suffered from water; Fu repeatedly managed the Jingou sea-outlet Jinzong River, the Beiyun Kuanggang diversion canal, and the Tongzhou Chaobai River, establishing civil and military flood-duty officials to assist defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin had long suffered floods; Zhou Fu repeatedly worked on the Jinzong outlet to the sea, the Kuanggang diversion on the Grand Canal, and the Chaobai River at Tongzhou, posting civil and military flood-control officers along them.

sentences.zh: 並言天津為九河故道，不洩則水患莫瘳，請就上游闢減河而開屯田，南運下游分水勢。

translations.literal: He also stated that Tianjin was the old course of the Nine Rivers—if not discharged, water calamity could not be cured—and requested opening diversion canals upstream while opening garrison farms, dividing the southern transport's downstream water force.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Tianjin lay in the old channel of the Nine Rivers and could not be relieved unless excess water was diverted upstream through new canals, with garrison farms opened and the Grand Canal current split downstream.

sentences.zh: 部議格不行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and blocked it from implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The Board rejected the plan.

sentences.zh: 後提督周盛傳開興濟減河，屯田小站，實本馥議。

translations.literal: Later Provincial Commander Zhou Shengchuan opened the Xingji diversion canal and garrison-farmed Xiaozhan—this in fact originated from Fu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Later Provincial Commander Zhou Shengchuan opened the Xingji diversion and garrison farms at Xiaozhan—implementing Zhou Fu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 丁艱，服除，署津海關道。

translations.literal: On bereavement leave, after mourning ended he acted as Tianjin Maritime Customs intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he served as acting intendant of the Tianjin Maritime Customs.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮初通商，馥與美提督薛裴爾議草商約保衛之，首稱朝鮮為中國屬邦，固以防侵奪也，而樞府削之。

translations.literal: When Korea first opened trade, Fu with American consul-general Shufeldt negotiated a draft commercial treaty to protect it, first calling Korea China's tributary state—solidly to guard against seizure—yet the Grand Council struck it out.
translations.idiomatic: When Korea first opened to trade, Zhou Fu drafted a commercial treaty with American Minister Shufeldt that explicitly called Korea a Chinese dependency—a safeguard against foreign seizure—but the Grand Council struck that clause.

sentences.zh: 馥私歎曰：「分義不著，禍始此矣！

translations.literal: Fu privately sighed: 'When status and obligation are not made clear, disaster begins from this!'
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu sighed in private: "When rights and obligations are left unclear, calamity starts here!"

sentences.zh: 」九年，兼署天津兵備道，俄真除津海關道。

translations.literal: ' In the ninth year he concurrently acted as Tianjin military preparedness intendant, and shortly received regular appointment as Tianjin Maritime Customs intendant.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1883 he also served as acting Tianjin military preparedness intendant, and soon received a regular appointment as Tianjin customs intendant.

sentences.zh: 中法事起，鴻章命赴海口編民舶立團防。

translations.literal: When the Sino-French affair arose, Hongzhang ordered him to go to Haikou to organize civilian vessels and establish community defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French War broke out, Li Hongzhang sent him to Haikou to organize merchant shipping into local defense corps.

sentences.zh: 鴻章之督畿輔也，先後垂三十年，創立海軍，自東三省、山東諸要塞皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Hongzhang's governorship of the capital region lasted nearly thirty years in all; he founded the navy, and from the Three Eastern Provinces and Shandong the various fortresses all belonged to it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang governed the metropolitan region for nearly thirty years, founded the navy, and brought fortresses from Manchuria and Shandong under its command.

sentences.zh: 用西法制造械器，輪電路礦，萬端並舉，尤加意海陸軍學校。

translations.literal: Using Western methods to manufacture weapons, steam, telegraph, railways, and mines—myriad undertakings launched together—he especially gave attention to naval and army schools.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced Western arms manufacture, steam, telegraph, railways, and mining on a broad scale, and paid special attention to naval and military academies.

sentences.zh: 北洋新政，稱盛一時，馥贊畫為多。

translations.literal: The Beiyang new policies were acclaimed flourishing for a time; Fu contributed planning to much of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiyang reforms were celebrated as a golden age, and Zhou Fu had a hand in much of the planning.

sentences.zh: 醇親王校閱海軍，嘉其勞，擢按察使。

translations.literal: Prince Chun reviewed the navy, praised his labor, and promoted him to provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chun inspected the navy he commended Zhou Fu's work and promoted him to provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再署布政使。

translations.literal: He again acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as acting provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 築永定河北岸石堤衛京師，盧溝南減水石壩工尤鉅，自是河不溢。

translations.literal: He built a stone dike on the Yongding River's north bank to guard the capital; the stone flood-reduction dam south of Lugou was especially large—from this the river did not overflow.
translations.idiomatic: He built a stone dike on the north bank of the Yongding to protect the capital, including a massive flood-reduction dam south of Lugou Bridge, and the river ceased to overflow.

sentences.zh: 中日開釁，馥任前敵營務處，跋涉安東、遼陽、摩天嶺之間，調護諸將，收集散亡，糧以不匱。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese war opened, Fu served at the forward camp affairs office, trudging between Andong, Liaoyang, and Motianling, coordinating and protecting the various generals, gathering the scattered and lost, so grain was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out with Japan, Zhou Fu ran the forward camp supply office, traveling between Andong, Liaoyang, and Motianling to support the generals, regroup stragglers, and keep provisions flowing.

sentences.zh: 和議成，乃自免歸。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, he then resigned of his own accord and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was signed he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 鴻章疏薦之，授四川布政使。

translations.literal: Hongzhang memorialized to recommend him and he was appointed Sichuan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang recommended him, and he was appointed provincial treasurer of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 至則課吏績，廣銀幣，積糧儲。

translations.literal: On arrival he assessed officials' performance, expanded silver currency, and accumulated grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he graded officials' performance, expanded silver coinage, and built up grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 慮教案易生釁，撰安輯民教示頒郡縣。

translations.literal: Fearing missionary cases easily gave rise to incidents, he drafted instructions for pacifying laymen and converts and promulgated them to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing missionary disputes, he drafted instructions on keeping peace between converts and the general population and sent them to every prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拳亂作，八國聯兵內犯，鴻章為議和大臣，總督直隸，馥亦調直隸布政使。

translations.literal: Before long the Boxer turmoil arose and the Eight-Nation Allied armies invaded inland; Hongzhang became peace negotiator and governor of Zhili, and Fu was also transferred to Zhili provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Boxer rising brought the allied powers inland; Li Hongzhang became peace negotiator and governor of Zhili, and Zhou Fu was transferred as Zhili provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 先隨鴻章入都，理京畿教案，數月事稍定，始赴保定受布政使印。

translations.literal: First he followed Hongzhang into the capital to handle metropolitan missionary cases; after several months matters were somewhat settled, and only then went to Baoding to receive the treasurer's seal.
translations.idiomatic: He first accompanied Li Hongzhang to Beijing to settle missionary cases in the capital region; after several months he went to Baoding to take up the treasurer's seal.

sentences.zh: 先是法兵至保定，戕前布政使廷雍，遂踞司署。

translations.literal: Earlier French troops had reached Baoding, killed the former treasurer Ting Yong, and then occupied the provincial office.
translations.idiomatic: French troops had earlier reached Baoding, killed Acting Treasurer Ting Yong, and occupied the provincial yamen.

sentences.zh: 及聞馥來，列隊郊迎入署。

translations.literal: When they heard Fu was coming, they formed ranks to welcome him at the suburbs and escort him into the office.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned Zhou Fu was coming, they lined up to welcome him outside the city and escorted him into the yamen.

sentences.zh: 久之，觀其設施，無間言，乃徐引去。

translations.literal: After a long while, observing his measures, with no dissenting words, they then slowly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After watching his administration for some time without complaint, they gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 鴻章卒，遂護直督。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang died, he thereupon acted as Zhili governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Hongzhang's death he served as acting governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 俄擢山東巡撫，詔留議津榆路事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted Shandong governor; an edict ordered him retained to deliberate the Tianjin–Luanzhou railway matter.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted governor of Shandong but kept in Beijing to negotiate the Tianjin–Luanzhou railway question.

sentences.zh: 時和議雖成，外國兵壁天津，踞津榆鐵道，設都統，治民政，屢爭莫能得。

translations.literal: At the time, though peace was concluded, foreign troops encamped at Tianjin, held the Tianjin–Luanzhou railway, established a general command, governed civil affairs—repeated disputes could not gain resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Although peace had been signed, foreign troops still held Tianjin and the Tianjin–Luanzhou railway under an allied council that ran local civil affairs, and repeated negotiations had failed.

sentences.zh: 至是，馥竟以片言解之。

translations.literal: At this point Fu actually resolved it with a few words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu settled the deadlock with a few words.

sentences.zh: 馥撫山東，值河決利津薄莊，議徙民居，不塞薄莊，俾河流直瀉抵海。

translations.literal: As Shandong governor, Fu encountered the Yellow River breaking at Lijin Bozhuang; he proposed moving residents, not blocking Bozhuang, so the river could pour straight to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Shandong, when the Yellow River burst at Lijin near Bozhuang, he proposed relocating residents and leaving the breach open so the river could run straight to the sea.

sentences.zh: 沿河設電局，備石工，訖十馀年，河不為災。

translations.literal: Along the river he established telegraph offices and prepared stone works; for more than ten years the river did not become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He set up telegraph stations along the river and stockpiled stone for repairs; for more than ten years the river caused no major disaster.

sentences.zh: 德踞膠州灣，築鐵道達省治，因佔路側礦山。

translations.literal: Germany occupied Jiaozhou Bay, built a railway reaching the provincial capital, and thereby seized mines along the line.
translations.idiomatic: Germany held Jiaozhou Bay, built a railway to the provincial capital, and seized mines along the route.

sentences.zh: 馥奏開濟南、周村商埠相箝制，德人意沮，自撤膠濟路兵，還五礦。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized to open treaty ports at Jinan and Zhoucun to counterbalance each other; German intentions were discouraged, they themselves withdrew Jiaoji railway troops, and returned five mines.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to open treaty ports at Jinan and Zhoucun as a counterweight; the Germans lost heart, withdrew troops from the Jiaoji line, and returned five mines.

sentences.zh: 馥既膺疆寄，則益欲大有為，凡所以阜民財、瀹民智者，次第興舉，天子嘉之，擢署兩江總督，移督兩廣。

translations.literal: Once Fu received frontier trust, he wished all the more to achieve great things; whatever could enrich popular wealth and enlighten popular wisdom he launched in sequence; the Son of Heaven praised him, promoted him to act as governor-general of the Two Jiangs, then transferred him to govern the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with a frontier post, Zhou Fu sought larger achievements, launching programs to enrich and enlighten the people in turn. The emperor commended him, appointed him acting governor-general of Jiangsu and Jiangxi, then transferred him to the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，請告歸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1907 he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 越十四年，卒，諡愨慎。

translations.literal: After fourteen years he died; posthumous title Que Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years later he died; his posthumous title was Queshen (Respectful Caution).

sentences.zh: 直隸、山東、江南士民皆祠祀之。

translations.literal: Officials and people of Zhili, Shandong, and Jiangnan all erected shrines to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Communities in Zhili, Shandong, and the lower Yangzi region all erected shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 陸元鼎，字春江，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanding, courtesy name Chunjiang, was a native of Renhe, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding, whose courtesy name was Chunjiang, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，以知縣即用，分山西，改江蘇。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, appointed directly as county magistrate, assigned to Shanxi, then changed to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of 1874, he was appointed directly as county magistrate, first assigned to Shanxi and then transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，權知山陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he acted as magistrate of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he served as acting magistrate of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 有姦豪民交通胥役，略人口行鬻，捕輒先遁。

translations.literal: There was a wicked powerful man who colluded with clerks and runners, abducted people and trafficked them; when arrested he always fled first.
translations.idiomatic: A local bully colluded with yamen clerks to kidnap people for sale; whenever officers came to arrest him he escaped first.

sentences.zh: 元鼎黎明起，盛儀從謁客，中道折至民家，破門入，縛治其豪，取出所略女婦數十人各放歸，驩聲雷動。

translations.literal: Yuanding rose at dawn, with grand retinue set out to visit a guest, midway turned to a commoner's house, broke the door and entered, bound and punished the bully, took out several tens of abducted women and released each to return; cheers thundered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Lu Yuanding set out with a grand procession as if to pay a formal visit, then suddenly turned into a private house, broke in, seized the bully, and freed dozens of kidnapped women; cheers erupted like thunder.

sentences.zh: 補江寧，以憂歸。

translations.literal: He filled the Jiangning post, then returned on bereavement leave.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to Jiangning but left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 服除，坐補原缺，調上海。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he resumed his original vacancy by seniority and was transferred to Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed his former rank and was transferred to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 法蘭西人擊殺縣人沈兆龍，傷隱不見，法領事不承擊殺。

translations.literal: A Frenchman beat and killed the county man Shen Zhaolong; the wound was hidden and not visible, and the French consul did not acknowledge the killing.
translations.idiomatic: A Frenchman beat Shen Zhaolong to death; the fatal wound was concealed, and the French consul denied murder.

sentences.zh: 元鼎曰：「時計表墜地，有鋼條內斷而磁面未損者，與此何以異？

translations.literal: Yuanding said: 'When a watch falls to the ground, there are cases where the steel spring breaks inside while the enamel face is undamaged—how is this different?'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding said: "When a watch falls, the mainspring can break inside while the dial looks intact—how is this case different?"

sentences.zh: 」領事語塞。

translations.literal: ' The consul was left speechless.
translations.idiomatic: " The consul had no reply.

sentences.zh: 如皋焚教堂，檄元鼎往視，教士聲言議不諧，當以兵戎見。

translations.literal: Rugao burned a church; an order summoned Yuanding to inspect; missionaries declared that if talks failed they would meet with armed force.
translations.idiomatic: When a church was burned at Rugao, Lu Yuanding was ordered to investigate; missionaries threatened war if negotiations failed.

sentences.zh: 元鼎曰：「如皋非軍艦所能至也。

translations.literal: Yuanding said: 'Rugao is not a place warships can reach.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding replied: "Warships cannot reach Rugao."

sentences.zh: 」不為動。

translations.literal: ' He was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: " He was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 抗議十馀日，乃定償銀四千，無他求。

translations.literal: After protesting more than ten days, they settled on four thousand taels compensation, with no other demands.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days of negotiation, indemnity was fixed at four thousand taels with no further demands.

sentences.zh: 是時江南北焚教堂十馀所，次第定議，悉視如皋。

translations.literal: At that time north and south of the river more than ten churches were burned; settlements were reached in sequence, all following the Rugao precedent.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten churches were burned north and south of the Yangzi; each case was settled on the Rugao model.

sentences.zh: 移知泰州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 城河久淤墊，歲旱，民苦無水。

translations.literal: The city moat had long been silted and filled; in a drought year the people suffered from lack of water.
translations.idiomatic: The city moat had long silted up; in a drought year the people lacked water.

sentences.zh: 元鼎濬治之，又移徙市廛迫河滸者，雖巨室無所徇。

translations.literal: Yuanding dredged and remedied it, and also moved market stalls pressing the riverbank—even great houses he did not favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding dredged it and relocated market stalls along the bank, showing no favor even to wealthy households.

sentences.zh: 下河斜豐港故有堤，在泰州境者六十里，入東台境，堤庳，水至勿能禦。

translations.literal: On the lower river the Xiefenggang had an old dike; within Taizhou territory it ran sixty li; entering Dongtai territory the dike was low, and when water came it could not be defended.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiefenggang dike ran sixty li through Taizhou; in Dongtai the embankment was so low that floodwaters could not be held back.

sentences.zh: 元鼎增高至十丈，廣如之，而豐其下以倍。

translations.literal: Yuanding raised it to ten zhang in height, as broad proportionally, and doubled the breadth at the base.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding raised it to ten zhang high and proportionally wide, with the base twice as broad.

sentences.zh: 工竟，按察使檄東台治堤與泰州接，元鼎又助工十有一里，自是兩境無水患。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, the judicial commissioner ordered Dongtai to repair the dike to join Taizhou's; Yuanding also assisted work for eleven li more—from this the two jurisdictions had no water calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done, the judicial commissioner ordered Dongtai to link its dike to Taizhou's; Lu Yuanding helped build another eleven li, and both districts were thereafter free of flooding.

sentences.zh: 尋調上元，援例以道員候選。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Shangyuan, and by precedent became a candidate for circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Shangyuan and, by precedent, became a candidate for circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督劉坤一疏薦元鼎才任方面，二十一年，授惠潮嘉道，調江蘇糧道，遷按察使。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Kunyi of the Two Jiangs memorialized recommending Yuanding's talent for frontier responsibility; in the twenty-first year he was appointed Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiaying Circuit intendant, transferred to Jiangsu grain transport intendant, and promoted judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Kunyi recommended Lu Yuanding for higher office; in 1895 he was appointed intendant of the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiaying Circuit, then grain intendant of Jiangsu, and promoted to judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陛見，溫語移時。

translations.literal: At imperial audience, warm words extended for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: At audience with the emperor he was addressed warmly for a long time.

sentences.zh: 論及前歲日本構戰，我軍槍彈多與口徑不合，以故敗。

translations.literal: Discussion turned to the previous year's Japanese war-making: our army's rifle bullets mostly did not match the bore caliber, and for this reason they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The conversation turned to the recent war with Japan: many army rifles and ammunition were mismatched in caliber, which was one reason for defeat.

sentences.zh: 帝因諭樞臣戒督撫審軍實，且曰：「毋謂語由元鼎，使督撫生芥蒂也。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon instructed Grand Council members to warn governors to examine military realities, and said: 'Do not say these words came from Yuanding and make governors bear a grudge.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Grand Council to warn governors to inspect their armies honestly, adding: "Do not let them think this came from Lu Yuanding and breed resentment."

sentences.zh: 」江陰焚教堂，縣吏捕首事者上之按察使。

translations.literal: ' At Jiangyin a church was burned; county officials arrested the ringleaders and sent them up to the judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " When a church was burned at Jiangyin, county officials arrested the ringleaders and sent them to the judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上海領事謂逮捕者非首犯，駐京公使言於總署，令領事往會鞫。

translations.literal: The Shanghai consul said those arrested were not the chief culprits; the minister in Beijing spoke to the Zongli Yamen, ordering the consul to go for joint trial.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanghai consul claimed the wrong men had been arrested; the minister in Beijing pressed the Zongli Yamen to let the consul join the trial.

sentences.zh: 元鼎曰：「會鞫有專官，按察使署非會鞫所。

translations.literal: Yuanding said: 'Joint trial has specialized officials; the judicial commissioner's office is not a joint-trial venue.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding replied: "Joint trials have designated officers; a judicial commissioner's yamen is not the place for them."

sentences.zh: 」領事言：「不會鞫，當觀讞也。

translations.literal: ' The consul said: 'If there is no joint trial, I should observe the judgment record.'
translations.idiomatic: " The consul said: "If there is no joint trial, I must at least see the verdict."

sentences.zh: 」元鼎持不可，領事曰：「其如總署指揮何？

translations.literal: ' Yuanding held firm that it could not be done; the consul said: 'But what of the Zongli Yamen's orders?'
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yuanding refused. The consul asked: "What about orders from the Zongli Yamen?"

sentences.zh: 」元鼎曰：「慎守國憲。

translations.literal: ' Yuanding said: 'Carefully uphold the national constitution.'
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yuanding answered: "Uphold the laws of the realm."

sentences.zh: 官可辭，法不可撓！

translations.literal: Office may be resigned; law cannot be bent!'
translations.idiomatic: An official may resign; the law cannot be bent!"

sentences.zh: 」領事怏怏去。

translations.literal: ' The consul left displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The consul withdrew in annoyance.

sentences.zh: 樞臣聞而嘉之，曰：「不爾，又為故事矣。

translations.literal: Grand Council members heard and praised it, saying: 'Otherwise, it would again become an old story.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Council members praised him, saying: "Otherwise we would have yielded as usual."

sentences.zh: 」尋署布政使，護巡撫。

translations.literal: ' Shortly he acted as provincial treasurer and protected the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon served as acting treasurer and acting governor.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷漕運總督，調湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to director-general of grain transport, then transferred as Hunan governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1903 he was appointed director-general of grain transport, then transferred as governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時方在告，廣西匪起，窺湖南，貴州匪逼靖州。

translations.literal: He was then on leave; Guangxi bandits rose and eyed Hunan, and Guizhou bandits pressed Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was on leave when bandits rose in Guangxi and threatened Hunan, while Guizhou rebels pressed Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元鼎力疾赴官，籌邊防，與總督張之洞會奏以堵為防，不如以助剿為防。

translations.literal: Yuanding, forcing himself despite illness, hurried to office, planned border defense, and with Governor-General Zhang Zhidong jointly memorialized that blocking as defense was inferior to aiding suppression as defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding took office despite illness, organized border defense, and with Governor-General Zhang Zhidong memorialized that sealing the border was less effective than helping suppress rebels across it.

sentences.zh: 於是募勇，令提督劉光才防西路，令衡永道莊賡良入貴州，而道員黃忠浩佐之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited braves, ordered Provincial Commander Liu Guangcai to defend the western route, ordered Hengyong Circuit Intendant Zhuang Gengliang to enter Guizhou with Circuit Intendant Huang Zhonghao assisting.
translations.idiomatic: He raised local militia, sent Provincial Commander Liu Guangcai to guard the western front, and sent Hengyong Intendant Zhuang Gengliang into Guizhou with Intendant Huang Zhonghao to assist.

sentences.zh: 賡良攻下龍貫峒，忠浩亦大敗悍賊於同樂。

translations.literal: Gengliang attacked and took Longguan Cave; Zhonghao also inflicted a great defeat on fierce bandits at Tongle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Gengliang captured Longguan Cave, and Huang Zhonghao routed fierce rebels at Tongle.

sentences.zh: 又令提督張慶雲助擊廣西四十八峒。

translations.literal: He also ordered Provincial Commander Zhang Qingyun to assist in attacking Guangxi's Forty-Eight Dong.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Provincial Commander Zhang Qingyun to help suppress the Forty-Eight Dong in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 亂徐定，朝命雲南布政使劉春霖移湖南，率所部滇軍助湘防。

translations.literal: The turmoil was gradually settled; the court ordered Yunnan Treasurer Liu Chunlin transferred to Hunan to lead his Yunnan troops in assisting Hunan defense.
translations.idiomatic: As order returned, the court transferred Yunnan Treasurer Liu Chunlin to Hunan with his Yunnan troops to reinforce the province.

sentences.zh: 元鼎言滇軍不可用，已而後營果叛。

translations.literal: Yuanding said the Yunnan army could not be used; before long the rear battalion indeed mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding warned that the Yunnan troops were unreliable; soon afterward the rear battalion mutinied as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 醴陵會匪謀叛事泄，自承革命，語連日本留學生。

translations.literal: The Liling secret-society bandits' plot to rebel was exposed; they themselves confessed revolution, words linking Japanese students abroad.
translations.idiomatic: A Liling secret-society plot to rebel was exposed; the conspirators confessed to revolutionary aims and implicated students in Japan.

sentences.zh: 元鼎誅二人，囚一人，他無所株連，人心大定。

translations.literal: Yuanding executed two, imprisoned one, and implicated no others; popular hearts were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanding executed two, imprisoned one, and implicated no one else; public order was quickly restored.

sentences.zh: 徵兵之議起也，元鼎已調撫江蘇。

translations.literal: When the conscription debate arose, Yuanding had already been transferred to govern Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: When debate over conscription arose, Lu Yuanding had already been transferred as governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 上言：「南人柔脆，其應徵者多市井無藉，不勝兵。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Southerners are soft and fragile; those who respond to conscription are mostly market-town riffraff, unfit for soldiery.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Southerners are not hardy; conscripts from the south are mostly idle townsmen unfit for soldiering."

sentences.zh: 當專選江北淮、徐諸府，不當限區域。

translations.literal: One should specially select from north-of-the-river Huai and Xu prefectures, and not limit by region.'
translations.idiomatic: Recruits should be drawn from Huai and Xu prefectures north of the Yangzi, not limited by province."

sentences.zh: 」部議格不行。

translations.literal: ' The ministry deliberated and blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Board rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 其後逃亡相屬，如元鼎言。

translations.literal: Afterward desertions followed one after another, just as Yuanding had said.
translations.idiomatic: Desertions followed, just as Lu Yuanding had warned.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，京察開缺另簡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, at the metropolitan personnel review his post was declared vacant and another appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1903, at the metropolitan personnel review, his post was declared vacant and another official appointed.

sentences.zh: 明年，召入京，奏對，語及江、浙爭滬杭鐵道事，元鼎力言士民忠愛無他心，上為動容。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to the capital, presented memorials in audience; talk touched the Jiang-Zhe dispute over the Shanghai-Hangzhou railway; Yuanding strongly stated that gentry and people were loyal and loving without other intent—the sovereign was moved.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to Beijing. Speaking of the Jiangsu-Zhejiang dispute over the Shanghai-Hangzhou railway, he insisted that local gentry and people were loyal patriots without hidden motives, and the emperor was moved.

sentences.zh: 命以三品京堂候補，佐辦資政院事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to await appointment as third-rank capital official and assist in managing Political Consultative Council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a third-rank capital official on probation to assist the Political Consultative Council.

sentences.zh: 俄，乞歸。

translations.literal: Shortly he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 1910.

sentences.zh: 張曾敭，字小帆，直隸南皮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Cengyang, courtesy name Xiaofan, was a native of Nanpi, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cengyang, whose courtesy name was Xiaofan, came from Nanpi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，以編修出知湖南永順府。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the seventh year of Tongzhi; as Hanlin compiler he went out to serve as prefect of Yongshun, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of 1868, he left the Hanlin Academy to serve as prefect of Yongshun in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 地屬苗疆，號難治。

translations.literal: The territory belonged to the Miao frontier and was called hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay in the Miao frontier and was considered difficult to govern.

sentences.zh: 斥貲募勇戢盜，悉置之法；

translations.literal: He spent his own funds to recruit braves to suppress bandits and placed them all under the law;
translations.idiomatic: He spent his own money to raise militia against bandits and punished every offender by law;

sentences.zh: 吏之尤貪污者，彈劾之。

translations.literal: officials who were especially corrupt he impeached.
translations.idiomatic: and impeached the most corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 徙知廣東肇慶府，有惠愛，督撫交章論薦。

translations.literal: Transferred to serve as prefect of Zhaoqing, Guangdong, he showed benevolent care; governor and governor-general sent successive memorials recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhaoqing in Guangdong, he won the people's affection, and his superiors repeatedly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，除福建鹽法道。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he was appointed Fujian salt-law circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was appointed intendant of Fujian salt administration.

sentences.zh: 閩鹽踴貴，私運蜂起。

translations.literal: Fujian salt soared in price and private transport swarmed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian salt prices soared and smuggling flourished.

sentences.zh: 為嚴立​​規約，奏免全釐以卹商，而正課亦饒。

translations.literal: He strictly established regulations, memorialized to exempt full levies to comfort merchants, and yet regular tax was also ample.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed strict regulations, memorialized to abolish surcharges to aid merchants, and still collected full regular revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷按察使，歲馀，病免。

translations.literal: Promoted to judicial commissioner; after more than a year, dismissed on illness.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to judicial commissioner, he resigned a year later on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 越三年，再起，召見，奏對稱旨，皇太后獎其明慎，即日授四川按察使，未到官，遷福建布政使。

translations.literal: After three years he was reappointed, received audience, memorialized in accord with imperial intent; the Empress Dowager praised his clarity and caution, the same day appointed Sichuan judicial commissioner—before reaching office, transferred to Fujian provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was recalled, impressed the court in audience, and was praised by the Empress Dowager for clarity and prudence. The same day he was named judicial commissioner of Sichuan, but before taking office was transferred to provincial treasurer of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 調廣西，桂故瘠區，又分任庚子賠款，益不支。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangxi—Gui was an old poor region, and also bore a share of the Gengzi indemnity—still more unable to sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangxi, an already poor province further burdened with its share of the Boxer indemnity, finances were stretched even thinner.

sentences.zh: 曾敭改釐章，嚴比較，裁冗費，罷不急官吏，用以不絀。

translations.literal: Cengyang revised the levy regulations, enforced strict comparison, cut redundant expenses, dismissed non-urgent officials and clerks, and thereby kept accounts from falling short.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang revised levy regulations, enforced strict audits, cut waste, dismissed nonessential officials, and kept the budget balanced.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Shanxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1903 he was appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 日俄釁作，日軍進駐遼南。

translations.literal: The Russo-Japanese quarrel arose; Japanese troops advanced and garrisoned southern Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Russo-Japanese War broke out, Japanese troops occupied southern Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 曾敭建議：「闢要地為商埠，別與日本密訂協守同盟之約，聲明不干內治。

translations.literal: Cengyang proposed: 'Open key places as treaty ports, separately with Japan secretly conclude a mutual-defense alliance treaty, declaring non-interference in internal government.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang proposed: "Open key points as treaty ports, conclude a secret mutual-defense alliance with Japan, and declare that internal administration would not be interfered with."

sentences.zh: 所慮者俄為日敗，必將取償於我；

translations.literal: What is feared is that Russia, defeated by Japan, will surely seek compensation from us;
translations.idiomatic: The concern was that Russia, defeated by Japan, would seek compensation from China;

sentences.zh: 伊犁鄰近籓封，亦漸外鄉，故亟宜籌餉練兵，有備無患；

translations.literal: Ili borders near the frontier seal and is also gradually turning outward—therefore one should urgently raise funds and train troops, prepared so there is no worry;
translations.idiomatic: Ili lay near the frontier and was drifting out of control, so funds and troops should be raised at once as a precaution;

sentences.zh: 而庫張鐵路可緩辦以伐其謀。

translations.literal: while the Kulun-Zhangjiakou railway can be delayed in construction to thwart their schemes.'
translations.idiomatic: and construction of the Kulun–Zhangjiakou railway could be delayed to frustrate Russian designs."

sentences.zh: 」言頗扼要。

translations.literal: ' The words were quite to the point.
translations.idiomatic: " The argument was concise and forceful.

sentences.zh: 馬賊劉天祐等擾後套，曾敭調集各軍討平之。

translations.literal: Horse bandits Liu Tianyou and others disturbed the Rear Banner; Cengyang mobilized various armies to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When horse bandits led by Liu Tianyou raided the Rear Banner, Zhang mobilized troops and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，調撫浙江。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to govern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 he was transferred as governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時浙西鹽梟煽熾，嘉湖統將吳家玉陰與梟通，都司范榮華尤不法。

translations.literal: At the time western Zhejiang salt smugglers flared fiercely; Jiahu commanding general Wu Jiayu secretly communicated with smugglers, and Battalion Commander Fan Ronghua was especially lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang was rife with salt smuggling; commanding general Wu Jiayu of Jiahu colluded with smugglers, and Battalion Commander Fan Ronghua was especially lawless.

sentences.zh: 曾敭便道之官，或勸以兵從，曰：「是速之叛也！

translations.literal: Cengyang took a shortcut to office; some urged him to take troops along, saying: 'That would hasten rebellion!'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang traveled light to take office; when advisers urged an armed escort, he said: "That would provoke rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 」遂輕騎迳嘉郡，召家玉入謁，諭以禍福，家玉不敢動，徐檄他將領其眾，而羈之甬東，僇榮華等，梟漸斂跡。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon with light cavalry he went straight to Jia Prefecture, summoned Jiayu to audience, instructed him on fortune and calamity—Jiayu dared not move; slowly he ordered another general to lead his troops, while detaining him east of Yong, punished Ronghua and others, and the smugglers gradually restrained their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: " He rode alone to Jiaxing, summoned Wu Jiayu, and warned him of the consequences; Wu did not dare move. Zhang then ordered another officer to take command of Wu's troops, detained Wu east of Ningbo, punished Fan Ronghua and others, and the smugglers gradually subsided.

sentences.zh: 浙路交涉久未決，草約逾定期，英領事猶堅執之。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang railway negotiations long went unsettled; the draft agreement passed its term, yet the British consul still stubbornly held to it.
translations.idiomatic: Negotiations over the Zhejiang railway dragged on; the draft treaty had expired, yet the British consul still insisted on it.

sentences.zh: 曾敭據約立爭，事乃定。

translations.literal: Cengyang argued on the basis of the treaty and matters were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang contested the case on treaty grounds, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，頒下法律大臣沈家本試行訴訟法，曾敭言：「中國禮教功用遠在法律上，是以尊親之義，載於禮經。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year Law Minister Shen Jiaben's trial civil procedure code was promulgated; Cengyang stated: 'China's ritual teaching's function far exceeds law; therefore the meaning of honoring kin is recorded in the Book of Rites.'
translations.idiomatic: In 1907 Law Minister Shen Jiaben's experimental civil procedure code was issued. Zhang argued: "In China ritual teaching outweighs statute; honoring parents is enshrined in the Book of Rites."

sentences.zh: 漢儒說論語，亦謂綱常為在所因，此各省所同，浙不能異者也。

translations.literal: Han Confucians explaining the Analects also said the constants of human relations are what one must rely on—this is the same in every province; Zhejiang cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: Han Confucian commentators on the Analects likewise held that moral constants must be upheld—this is true in every province, and Zhejiang cannot be an exception.

sentences.zh: 浙西梟匪出沒，浙東寇盜潛滋。

translations.literal: Western Zhejiang smuggler-bandits appear and vanish; eastern Zhejiang robbers and thieves secretly multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Smugglers haunted western Zhejiang while banditry quietly spread in the east.

sentences.zh: 治亂國用重典，猶懼不勝，驟改從輕，何以為治？

translations.literal: In governing disorder one uses severe statutes and still fears not prevailing—if one suddenly changes to leniency, how can one govern?
translations.idiomatic: A troubled country needs severe laws and even then may not prevail—how can sudden leniency restore order?

sentences.zh: 此他省或可行，而浙獨難行者也。

translations.literal: This other provinces might be able to implement, but Zhejiang alone finds hard to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Other provinces might manage this, but Zhejiang could not.

sentences.zh: 」於是逐條駁議之。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he rebutted and debated it article by article.
translations.idiomatic: " He then rebutted the code article by article.

sentences.zh: 是年秋瑾案起。

translations.literal: That year the Qiu Jin case arose.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Qiu Jin affair broke out.

sentences.zh: 秋瑾者，浙江女生言革命者也，留學日本，歸為紹興大通學校教師，陰謀亂。

translations.literal: Qiu Jin was a Zhejiang woman who advocated revolution; she studied in Japan, returned to serve as teacher at Shaoxing Datong School, and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jin was a Zhejiang woman revolutionary who had studied in Japan, returned to teach at Shaoxing's Datong School, and plotted rebellion in secret.

sentences.zh: 曾敭遣兵至校捕之，得其左驗，論重闢，黨人大譁。

translations.literal: Cengyang sent troops to the school to arrest her, obtained corroborating evidence, sentenced her to severe execution; party members raised a great outcry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sent troops to arrest her at the school, found incriminating evidence, and sentenced her to death; revolutionaries protested loudly.

sentences.zh: 調撫江蘇，俄調山西，稱疾歸。

translations.literal: Transferred to govern Jiangsu, shortly transferred to Shanxi, pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangsu, then soon to Shanxi, and retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 家居十四年，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He lived at home fourteen years, then died at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for fourteen years and died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 楊士驤，字蓮府，安徽泗州人。

translations.literal: Yang Shixiang, courtesy name Lianfu, was a native of Sizhou, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shixiang, whose courtesy name was Lianfu, came from Sizhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the twelfth year of Guangxu, selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of 1886, he entered the Hanlin Academy and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 保道員，補直隸通永道，擢按察使，遷江西布政使，復調直隸。

translations.literal: Promoted to circuit intendant, filled Zhili Tongyong Circuit, promoted judicial commissioner, transferred to Jiangxi provincial treasurer, again transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to circuit intendant, he served on the Tongyong Circuit in Zhili, became judicial commissioner, provincial treasurer of Jiangxi, and returned to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，署山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he acted as Shandong governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 he served as acting governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 河貫東省千馀裡，淤高而堤薄，歲漫決為巨害。

translations.literal: The river ran through the province more than a thousand li, silted high while dikes were thin—yearly breaches were a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River ran more than a thousand li through Shandong; the channel had silted up while the dikes were thin, and annual breaches were a major disaster.

sentences.zh: 士驤以為河所以歲決者，河工員吏利興修，又因以遷擢也。

translations.literal: Shixiang held that the reason the river yearly breached was that river-work officials and clerks profited from construction projects and also used them for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yang believed annual breaches persisted because river officials profited from repair projects and used them to win promotion.

sentences.zh: 乃定章程：歲安瀾，官奏敘，弁兵支款如例；

translations.literal: He thereupon fixed regulations: if the year was calm, officials memorialized for merit citation and officers and soldiers received funds as usual;
translations.idiomatic: He instituted rules: in a calm year officials could claim merit and troops received standard pay;

sentences.zh: 河決，官嚴參，不得留工效力，弁兵依律論斬。

translations.literal: if the river breached, officials were severely impeached, could not remain on the works to atone, and officers and soldiers were sentenced to decapitation by law.
translations.idiomatic: if the river breached, officials were severely punished, could not remain on the works to redeem themselves, and officers and soldiers faced capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 身巡河堤，厲賞罰，自是數年，山東無河患。

translations.literal: He personally inspected river dikes, enforced rewards and punishments—from this for several years Shandong had no river calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the dikes in person and enforced strict rewards and punishments; for several years thereafter Shandong had no major flood.

sentences.zh: 曹州多盜，行清鄉法，嚴督捕。

translations.literal: Caozhou had many bandits; he implemented rural pacification methods and strictly supervised arrests.
