translations.idiomatic: Caozhou was bandit-ridden; he applied rural pacification measures and pressed arrests vigorously.

sentences.zh: 德兵違約，屯膠、高，久不撤。

translations.literal: German troops violated the treaty, encamped at Jiao and Gao, and long did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: German troops violated their agreement and camped at Jiaozhou and Gaomi without withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 數月盜少戢，會各國撤京、津兵，士驤與德官議，遂盡撤駐路德兵。

translations.literal: Within several months bandits somewhat subsided; it happened that the various powers withdrew Beijing and Tianjin troops—Shixiang negotiated with German officials, and thereupon all German troops garrisoning the railway were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry eased within months; when the powers withdrew troops from Beijing and Tianjin, Yang negotiated with German officers and secured the full withdrawal of German forces along the railway.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，代袁世凱為直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he replaced Yuan Shikai as Zhili governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1907 he succeeded Yuan Shikai as governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 世凱為政，首練軍籌款，尤多興革，務樹威信，北洋大臣遂為中外所屬目。

translations.literal: Shikai in government first trained troops and raised funds, especially many innovations and abolitions, striving to plant authority and trust—the Beiyang minister thus became what Chinese and foreigners alike fixed their eyes upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had prioritized army training and fundraising, launched many reforms, and built authority, making the Beiyang governor-general the focus of domestic and foreign attention.

sentences.zh: 士驤承其後，一切奉行罔有違，財政日竭，難乎為繼，而周旋因應，常若有馀，時頗稱之。

translations.literal: Shixiang succeeded him, carried out everything without violation, yet finances daily exhausted and hard to continue—yet in social maneuvering and adaptation he often seemed to have surplus; at the time he was rather praised.
translations.idiomatic: Yang followed him, maintained all his policies, and though finances grew exhausted and hard to sustain, he handled affairs with apparent ease and won contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 明年，入覲。

translations.literal: The next year he entered for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he had an audience with the throne.

sentences.zh: 時議修永定河，士驤閱河工，疏言：「全河受病，一由下口高仰，宣洩不暢；

translations.literal: At the time they discussed repairing the Yongding River; Shixiang inspected river works and memorialized: 'The whole river suffers illness—first, because the lower mouth is high and tilted upward, discharge is not smooth;
translations.idiomatic: When repair of the Yongding River was debated, Yang inspected the works and memorialized: "The river's ailments are twofold: the lower outlet is elevated and blocked, preventing discharge;

sentences.zh: 一由減壩失修，分消無路。

translations.literal: second, because flood-reduction dams were not repaired and there was no route for divided discharge.'
translations.idiomatic: and the flood-reduction dams have fallen into disrepair, leaving no channel for overflow."

sentences.zh: 」盧溝橋以下舊有減壩，年久淤閉，宜折修，並​​挑減河，因請撥帑四十六萬馀兩。

translations.literal: ' Below Lugou Bridge there were old flood-reduction dams, silted and closed for years—they should be rebuilt in sections, and diversion canals dredged; he therefore requested an allocation of more than 460,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: " Below Lugou Bridge the old flood-reduction dams had silted shut; they should be rebuilt and diversion canals dredged, and he requested more than 460,000 taels from the treasury."

sentences.zh: 詔下部議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministry to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Board to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，德宗梓宮奉移西陵，詔所需不得攤派民間。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, Emperor Dezong's coffin was moved in honor to the Western Tombs; an edict declared required expenses must not be apportioned to the populace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909, when Emperor Guangxu's coffin was moved to the Western Tombs, an edict forbade levying the costs on the people.

sentences.zh: 士驤慨然思革百年之弊，疏曰：「國初因明季加派紛繁，民生彫敝，屢降旨申禁科累。

translations.literal: Shixiang, moved with resolve to reform a century's abuses, memorialized: 'At the dynasty's founding, because of the Ming season's many added levies, popular livelihood was carved and exhausted—repeated edicts forbade cumulative exactions.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang resolved to reform abuses of a century and memorialized: "At the founding of the dynasty, the many surcharges of the late Ming had exhausted the people, and repeated edicts forbade cumulative exactions."

sentences.zh: 近畿繁劇，供億多，不能盡革，故田賦較各省輕，而歲出差徭逾於糧銀之數。

translations.literal: The metropolitan region is busy and complex, supplies numerous—could not fully reform; therefore land tax is lighter than other provinces, yet yearly corvée levies exceed the grain-tax silver amount.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region remained complex and costly, so land tax stayed lighter than in other provinces, yet annual labor levies exceeded the grain tax in silver.

sentences.zh: 新政迭興，學堂、巡警諸費，無不取給於民，輸納之艱，日以加甚。

translations.literal: New policies arose in succession—schools, constabulary, and other expenses all drew supply from the people; the hardship of payment daily grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: With successive new policies, school and police costs and more were all levied on the people, and payment grew harder by the day.

sentences.zh: 擬官紳合查常年應官差徭，實係公用者，酌定數目，折交州縣自辦，不得濫派折錢；

translations.literal: It is proposed that officials and gentry jointly investigate yearly corvée due to government, what is truly for public use—fix the amount, convert and hand to prefectures and counties to manage themselves, and not permit reckless apportionment of cash conversion;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that officials and gentry audit annual public corvée, fix the amounts truly needed for public use, pay a cash commutation to prefectures and counties to handle themselves, and forbid reckless surcharges;

sentences.zh: 胥役書差，官給津貼。

translations.literal: runners, clerks, and document handlers—officials should provide allowances.
translations.idiomatic: with yamen runners and clerks paid official allowances.

sentences.zh: 庶積弊一清，上下交益。

translations.literal: Thus accumulated abuses may be cleared at once, and above and below mutually benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus long-standing abuses might be cleared and both government and people would benefit."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，優詔答之。

translations.literal: ' The memorial entered and received a favorable edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was answered with a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 五月，卒，贈太子少保，諡文敬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he died; posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Wenjing (Cultivated Respect).

sentences.zh: 士驤少孤露，起家幕僚，至於專閫，與人無迕，眾皆稱其通敏雲。

translations.literal: Shixiang in youth was orphaned and exposed, rose from staff service to frontier command, had no conflict with others—all praised his versatile quickness, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yang rose from secretarial work to frontier command, offended no one, and was widely praised for his tact and quick wit.

sentences.zh: 馮煦，字夢華，江蘇金壇人。

translations.literal: Feng Xu, courtesy name Menghua, was a native of Jintan, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xu, whose courtesy name was Menghua, came from Jintan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he was metropolitan graduate of the first class, top three, and appointed Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886 he placed among the top three metropolitan graduates of the first class and was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 疊上疏代奏，請圖自強，敦大本，行實政，德宗嘉納。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he submitted memorials by proxy memorialization, requesting plans for self-strengthening, honoring the great foundation, and carrying out practical government—Emperor Dezong commended and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized for national self-strengthening, sound fundamentals, and practical government; Emperor Guangxu approved.

sentences.zh: 典湖南鄉試，稱得士。

translations.literal: He presided over the Hunan provincial examination and was said to have obtained worthy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As chief examiner of the Hunan provincial examinations, he was praised for selecting able candidates.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以京察一等授安徽鳳陽知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, through metropolitan personnel review of the first grade he was appointed Fengyang prefect of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895, rated first class in the metropolitan personnel review, he was appointed prefect of Fengyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 鳳屬連年水澇，煦單騎按部，逐一履勘，以被災之重輕，定給賑之多寡，人霑實惠。

translations.literal: Fengyang territory suffered flood and waterlogging year after year; Xu rode alone on inspection, examined each place in turn, and according to the severity of disaster fixed the amount of relief—people received real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang suffered floods year after year; Feng rode alone through the district, inspected each area, and scaled relief to the severity of damage so that people received real help.

sentences.zh: 並屢平反疑獄。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly reversed doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly overturned wrongful convictions in doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 總督劉坤一以心存利濟、政切先勞疏保，兩攝鳳潁六泗道。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Kunyi memorialized to recommend him for mind set on benefiting others and government earnest in taking hardship first; twice he acted as Fengying-Liusi Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Kunyi recommended him for devoted public service and twice had him act as intendant of the Fengying-Liusi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷山西按察使，調四川。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Shanxi judicial commissioner, then to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1901 he was transferred to judicial commissioner of Shanxi, then to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 廣安州有聚眾謀毀學堂者，獲四人，擬照土匪例正法。

translations.literal: In Guang'an Prefecture men gathered plotting to destroy a school; four were seized and it was proposed to execute them by the bandit precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At Guang'an Prefecture a crowd plotted to destroy a school; four were arrested and the provincial government proposed executing them under the bandit law.

sentences.zh: 煦白大府，請按而後誅，以去就爭，至免冠抵幾，不得請不止。

translations.literal: Xu informed the superior office, requesting trial before execution; he contested with his post at stake, even removing his cap and striking the desk—he would not stop until his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Feng appealed to the provincial government for trial before execution, staking his office on the point, even removing his cap and pounding the desk until his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 旋署布政使，復調安徽，兼署提學使。

translations.literal: Shortly he acted as provincial treasurer, again transferred to Anhui, concurrently acting as education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting provincial treasurer, returned to Anhui, and also acted as education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was promoted governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1907 he was promoted governor.

sentences.zh: 時國是日非，海內外黨人昌言革命。

translations.literal: At the time national affairs daily worsened; revolutionaries at home and abroad loudly proclaimed revolution.
translations.idiomatic: National affairs were deteriorating daily, and revolutionaries at home and abroad openly preached revolution.

sentences.zh: 巡撫恩銘被刺，眾情惶惑。

translations.literal: Governor En Ming was assassinated and popular sentiment was fearful and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Governor En Ming was assassinated, and the public was shaken.

sentences.zh: 煦繼任，處以鎮靜，治其獄，不株連一人，主散脅從，示寬大，人心始安。

translations.literal: Xu succeeded to office, handled matters with calm, tried the case, implicated not a single other person, advocated dispersing followers, showed leniency—popular hearts only then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Feng succeeded him, acted calmly, tried the case without implicating others, urged leniency toward followers, and gradually restored public confidence.

sentences.zh: 复疏言：「今者黨禍已亟，民生不聊。

translations.literal: Again he memorialized: 'Now party calamity is already urgent, and popular livelihood has no relief.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "Party strife has become acute and the people's livelihood is desperate."

sentences.zh: 中外大臣不思引咎自責，合力圖強，乃粉飾因循，苟安旦夕，貽誤將來，大局阽危，日甚一日。

translations.literal: Chinese and foreign ministers do not think to accept blame and reproach themselves, join strength to seek vigor—instead they ornament and cover, follow old ways, seek peace for a day and night, entrust error to the future; the great situation teeters on peril, worse day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers at court and abroad neither accept blame nor unite to strengthen the state; they paper over problems, cling to routine, and seek a day's peace while the empire grows more perilous by the day.

sentences.zh: 挽救之方，唯以覈名實、明賞罰為第一義，而其要則在'民為邦本'一言。

translations.literal: The method of rescue lies solely in verifying name and reality and clarifying rewards and punishments as the first principle—and its key lies in the one phrase 'the people are the foundation of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Salvation lies first in matching names to realities and enforcing clear rewards and punishments—and above all in the principle that the people are the foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 有尊主庇民之臣，用之勿疑；

translations.literal: Where there are ministers who honor the ruler and shelter the people, employ them without doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Employ without hesitation ministers who honor the throne and protect the people;

sentences.zh: 有誤國殃民之臣，刑之毋赦。

translations.literal: where there are ministers who harm the state and bring calamity on the people, punish them without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: and punish without mercy those who harm the state and injure the people.

sentences.zh: 政府能使天下自治，則天下莫能亂；

translations.literal: If government can make the realm self-govern, then the realm cannot be thrown into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: If the government can make the realm govern itself, no one can throw it into chaos;

sentences.zh: 政府能使天下舉安，則天下莫能危。

translations.literal: if government can make the realm all secure, then the realm cannot be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: if it can make the realm secure as a whole, no one can endanger it.

sentences.zh: 根本大計，實係於此。

translations.literal: The fundamental great plan truly hinges on this.'
translations.idiomatic: The fundamental policy truly rests on this."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，大臣權幸多忌嫉之。

translations.literal: ' The memorial entered; powerful favored ministers mostly envied and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial angered many powerful courtiers.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂罷。

translations.literal: The next year he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，江、皖大水，復起為查賑大臣，出入災區，規定辦法，施及豫東，未一年，凡賑三十九州縣，放款至三百馀萬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong, Jiang and Wan suffered great floods; he was again raised as relief-inspection minister, went in and out of disaster zones, fixed methods, extended to eastern Henan—in less than a year he relieved thirty-nine prefectures and counties, disbursing loans to more than three million.
translations.idiomatic: In 1910, after great floods in Jiangsu and Anhui, he was again appointed relief commissioner, traveled through the disaster areas, set procedures, and extended aid into eastern Henan; within a year he relieved thirty-nine prefectures and counties and disbursed more than three million taels in loans.

sentences.zh: 後復立義賑會。

translations.literal: Later he again established a charitable relief society.
translations.idiomatic: He later founded a charitable relief society as well.

sentences.zh: 連年水旱，兼有兵災，遠而推至京、直、魯、豫、湘、浙，無歲不災，無災不賑，蓋自蒞官訖致仕，逮於耄老，與荒政相終始，眾稱善人。

translations.literal: Year after year flood and drought, together with military calamity—extending far to Beijing, Zhili, Shandong, Henan, Hunan, Zhejiang—no year without disaster, no disaster without relief; from taking office until retirement, down to great old age, he was with famine administration from start to finish; all called him a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Floods, droughts, and wars followed one another from the capital through Zhili, Shandong, Henan, Hunan, and Zhejiang; scarcely a year passed without disaster or relief work. From his first office to retirement and old age, famine relief was the thread of his career, and he was widely called a good man.

sentences.zh: 聞國變，痛哭失聲。

translations.literal: On hearing the national transformation, he wept bitterly and lost his voice.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the dynastic collapse, he wept until he could not speak.

sentences.zh: 越十有五年，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: After more than fifteen years he died at age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later he died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 煦居官廉而好施。

translations.literal: In office Xu was incorrupt and fond of giving.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was incorrupt in office and generous in charity.

sentences.zh: 平素講學，以有恥為的，重躬行實踐。

translations.literal: In ordinary times he lectured on learning, taking having shame as the target, emphasizing personal practice and real conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on learning, taking moral shame as his aim and stressing practice over theory.

sentences.zh: 文章爾雅，晚境至鬻文自給雲。

translations.literal: His writings were refined and elegant; in late years he even sold essays to support himself, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was refined; in his last years he is said to have supported himself by selling his writing.

sentences.zh: 論曰：光緒初，督撫權重，及其末年，中央集權，復多設法令以牽制之，吏治不可言矣。

translations.literal: The critique states: Early in Guangxu, governors-general and governors held heavy power; by its last years central power was concentrated, and moreover many laws and orders were set up to restrain them—civil administration cannot be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Early in the Guangxu reign governors held great power; by its end the court centralized authority and multiplied regulations to restrain them—administration was beyond repair.

sentences.zh: 錫良強直負重，安內攘外，頗有建樹。

translations.literal: Xi Liang was strong and upright, bore heavy responsibility, pacified within and repelled without—he had considerable achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang was upright and bore heavy responsibilities, pacifying internal troubles and resisting foreign pressure, with notable achievements.

sentences.zh: 馥諳練，士驤通敏，元鼎辦交涉，曾敭論法律，並能持正。

translations.literal: Fu was practiced and skilled, Shixiang versatile and quick, Yuanding handled negotiations, Cengyang discoursed on law—all able to hold to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu was experienced, Yang Shixiang tactful, Lu Yuanding handled foreign affairs, and Zhang Cengyang debated law—all upheld integrity.

sentences.zh: 煦善治賑，與荒政相終始。

translations.literal: Xu was good at managing relief and was with famine administration from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Feng excelled at famine relief throughout his career.

sentences.zh: 「民為邦本」，善哉言乎！

translations.literal: 'The people are the foundation of the state'—excellent words indeed!
translations.idiomatic: "The people are the foundation of the state"—well said indeed!

sentences.zh: 錫良初疏諫集權，樞廷轉相箝制。

translations.literal: Xi Liang at first memorialized remonstrating against centralization; the Grand Council in turn mutually obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Liang had early warned against centralization, yet the Grand Council obstructed him in turn.

sentences.zh: 及事變起，大勢所趨，皆一如所言，世尤服其先見雲。

translations.literal: When incidents arose, the trend of the great situation all matched what he had said—the age especially admired his foresight, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis came, events unfolded just as he had warned, and the world especially admired his foresight.
